principles: SWINGWELL must not consume time that could otherwise be spent playing or practicing golf.
The purpose of SWINGWELL is to become a better golfer without sacrificing the joy of playing golf.
Raise the floor, preserve the ceiling.

pillars.name: Ball Striking
pillars.outcome: Predictable low point and centered contact across the bag.

commitments.text: Consistently control the low point ahead of the ball.
Produce centered clubface contact across the irons.
Maintain effective pressure transfer through impact.
Establish a repeatable setup and ball position for each club.
Maintain consistent contact quality across successive shots.
Transfer reliable contact from partial swings to full swings.
Preserve contact quality when changing clubs and targets.
Reduce costly thin, fat and other contact errors during rounds.

pillars.performance_guidance: Initial practice benchmark: at least 8 of 10 acceptable contacts in a randomized iron set; define acceptable contact before testing.

pillars.name: Approach Play
pillars.outcome: Predictable approach shots that increase GIR, especially from 150–180 yards.

commitments.text: Establish reliable carry-distance windows for short and mid irons.
Establish reliable carry and dispersion windows for long-approach clubs, including hybrids and fairway woods.
Control distance dispersion to reduce approaches finishing significantly short or long.
Control lateral dispersion to keep intended greens within a realistic shot pattern.
Maintain accurate, evidence-based carry distances for all approach clubs.
Select clubs and targets using actual carry distances and expected dispersion.
Maintain approach accuracy when switching clubs, distances and targets.
Improve on-course greens in regulation, particularly from 150–180 yards.

pillars.performance_guidance: Initial GIR benchmark: 3 per 9 holes. Long-approach calibration: 7 of 10 within agreed carry and lateral windows; define windows by distance/club. Track 5i, 6i, 7i, 8i, 4H, 3W and future fairway woods as supporting evidence, not separate commitments.

pillars.name: Driving
pillars.outcome: Reliable, efficient driver distance while minimizing costly misses.

commitments.text: Establish a repeatable driver setup and alignment.
Develop a predictable driver starting direction and shot pattern.
Control clubface delivery to reduce significant left/right misses.
Maintain centered contact and efficient energy transfer.
Develop sustainable clubhead speed without sacrificing control.
Increase useful driving distance while maintaining playable dispersion.
Transfer driver reliability from practice to actual course conditions.
Reduce penalties, recovery shots and costly execution errors from driver tee shots.

pillars.performance_guidance: Development goals: 240–250 yards total, 95+ mph controlled speed; at least 80% playable driver tee shots; zero driver penalties per nine holes. Do not impose driver usage quota. Alternative tee-club selection belongs in Course Management.

pillars.name: Short Game
pillars.outcome: Turn missed greens into manageable bogeys and realistic par opportunities.

commitments.text: Produce consistent contact and predictable rollout on basic chips.
Control carry distance and trajectory on pitch shots.
Develop reliable greenside bunker escapes, with predictable distance and enough control to create putting opportunities.
Select appropriate short-game shots based on lie, landing area and available green.
Control landing spots and rollout across different clubs and trajectories.
Maintain effective short-game execution from rough, tight lies, uneven ground and other challenging conditions outside bunkers.
Transfer short-game skills from controlled practice to randomized, on-course situations.
Improve scrambling performance and eliminate costly short-game execution errors.

pillars.performance_guidance: Initial development benchmarks: scrambling at least 30%; 7 of 10 basic chips inside 6 feet from a defined lie; 9 of 10 bunker escapes safely onto green; at most one costly short-game mishit per nine holes. Bunker and non-bunker difficult lies are distinct.

pillars.name: Putting
pillars.outcome: Measurable, repeatable putting across distances, slopes and playing conditions, minimizing avoidable strokes.

commitments.text: Establish a repeatable setup and starting line.
Develop consistent pace control across putting distances.
Maintain reliable conversion inside five feet.
Improve conversion consistency from five to ten feet.
Establish conversion and distance-control performance from ten to fifteen feet.
Develop reliable lag putting from longer distances.
Read and execute putts across slopes, breaks and changing speeds.
Transfer putting performance to the course and minimize three-putts.

pillars.performance_guidance: Baseline first, no premature conversion percentages. Use established clock routine, long-lag test and sloped shelf. Aim for zero three-putts per nine; record first-putt leave and second-putt conversion. Flat green for calibration; slopes and random holes for transfer.

pillars.name: Course Management
pillars.outcome: Choose shots that reduce avoidable strokes and keep difficult holes manageable.

commitments.text: Select tee clubs based on landing-area width, hazards and expected dispersion.
Choose approach targets that account for shot patterns and trouble around the green.
Make club selections using reliable carry distances rather than maximum distances.
Evaluate risk and reward before attempting aggressive or low-percentage shots.
Choose recovery shots that restore a playable position without compounding errors.
Adapt shot selection to wind, elevation, lie and course conditions.
Maintain a consistent pre-shot decision process and commit to the selected shot.
Review costly scoring errors to distinguish poor decisions from poor execution.

pillars.performance_guidance: Initial goals: zero penalty strokes per nine; at most one costly execution error per nine across all clubs; zero compounded errors. Baseline decision quality separately from execution. Decision evaluation uses information available before shot. Mental commitment mechanics belong to P7.

pillars.name: Mental Game
pillars.outcome: Play with freedom, curiosity, gratitude and commitment; preserve enjoyment regardless of score.

commitments.text: Recognize my mental state (GREEN / YELLOW / RED) without judgment or attachment.
Maintain a regular mindfulness practice that develops awareness, perspective and emotional flexibility.
Execute a consistent pre-shot mental routine and commit fully to the selected shot.
Trust my swing without introducing last-second mechanical corrections.
Respond to poor shots with curiosity and problem-solving rather than frustration.
Maintain perspective and composure under pressure, uncertainty or unexpected outcomes.
Appreciate the opportunity to play, the course and the company regardless of score.
Reflect on each round with curiosity and gratitude, identifying lessons without self-criticism.

pillars.performance_guidance: Mindfulness/meditation (Calm or other approach) as regular practice, not a fifth range session. Post-round gratitude → curiosity → learning. Do not demand perfect happiness or suppress normal emotions; practice responding constructively.

pillars.name: Practice Discipline
pillars.outcome: Practice deliberately, measure honestly, and improve without making golf another job.

commitments.text: Maintain a realistic four-session weekly Flight Plan, adapting to available time and conditions.
Begin each practice session with a clear purpose and process-based intention.
Use measurable success criteria to distinguish improvement from repetition.
Balance technical development, randomized practice and on-course transfer.
Record every completed practice session and round in the SWINGWELL diary, with detail proportional to the evidence and learning value.
Complete the Saturday Review to identify progress, inconsistencies and emerging priorities.
Complete the Sunday Plan to translate findings into the next four-session Flight Plan.
Complete the Monthly Matrix Update to keep commitments and priorities aligned with the handicap objective.

pillars.performance_guidance: Four sessions are a planning baseline, not a quota. Record every completed practice and round, in brief when appropriate; no backlog or guilt. Saturday learn, Sunday prepare, monthly align.

outputs: Versioned matrix if evidence justifies change

priority_review.theme: Reliable approaches with a committed swing.
priority_review.note: Initial priorities approved by Ian. Review at the next Saturday Review; colors do not automatically expire or grade performance. The practice and review ceremonies remain standing operating commitments.
